subject: Dedicated GPU capacity – post-discovery summary & ops handoff
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@heliox.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap from today's capacity call

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for running through the platform this morning — the demo was helpful.  A quick recap from our side so we're aligned before you send a follow-up: 

- Primary goal: move inference for our core clinical triage model off local hosts to a reserved GPU pool to reduce maintenance overhead and get predictable latency.
- Current baseline: 12k daily requests, 99th p95 ~600ms on CPU + occasional OOMs during spikes.
- Target SLA: 99th token latency below 400ms for our 2k-token peak sequences; sustained throughput target ~2500 tokens/sec.
- Isolation needs: PHI-containing payloads, so tenant isolation + VPC-only access required.
- Scaling: predictable ramp to 3x traffic over 6 months (start with a pool sized for peak with burst policy).

Procurement: procurement@heliox.ai is the owner — they prefer a single PO and net-60 terms.

Can you send a short ops / sizing / SLA proposal and a ballpark cost so we can kick-off procurement? Also copy whoever owns on-call runbooks for onboarding.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of ML Infrastructure
Heliox AI

---
Attachment: Heliox-discovery-notes.pdf (stub)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@heliox.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's capacity call

Olivia — thanks for the clear summary and for surfacing procurement details.  Following up with a concise ops + commercial handoff below and next steps.

Recap / assumptions (from call):
- Model shape: ~2k average sequence length for peak requests; KV cache will be used for recurring prefixes (we estimated cache hit ~25%).
- Expected QPS profile: steady 4-6 rps average, spiking to ~20 rps for short windows (1-3 minutes).
- Data sensitivity: PHI; require VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for keys.

Proposed dedicated configuration (ballpark):
- Reserved pool: 4x NVIDIA H100 equivalent GPUs (fractional-containerized pools for multi-tenancy control).
- Isolation: single-tenant pool with dedicated node scheduling, VPC egress control, and per-route ACLs.
- Throughput/latency: target ~300–400ms 99th for your 2k sequence workload using condensed batching + 8-token streaming.
- Burst policy: add 50% on-call burst capacity for scheduled ramp windows and overprovision guardrails.
- Reliability: 99.5% uptime SLA, with automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant (8-bit quant) if primary pool is degraded.

Ops handoff items (deliverables we will provide):
- Engineering runbook: provisioning, canary deployment steps, KV cache warmup playbook.
- Acceptance test harness: synthetic workload to validate 99th token latency and throughput.
- On-call runbook + escalation path to Redwood SRE.

Attachments: I've included an initial MAP (attached) that maps your traffic to pool sizing and a draft SLA for procurement to review.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Procurement contact: please confirm final email for procurement (you listed procurement@heliox.ai).
2) Timeline: confirm whether you want a June 14th or June 28th provisioning start (we can meet either but lead time affects pricing).
3) Acceptance criteria: confirm the 99th-token latency target of 400ms (or confirm a different target).

I'll loop Marissa here to propose the commercial terms and a PO-friendly summary. Aditya will own onboarding ops once the PO is in.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Heliox-MAP-v1.xlsx (sizing workbook), SLA-DRAFT-Heliox-Redwood.pdf (draft)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@heliox.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's capacity call

Hi Olivia — looping in commercial details and a clear PO-ready summary.  Thanks Nikhil for the ops breakdown.

Commercial summary (ballpark, for procurement review):
- Commitment: Monthly reserved pool of 4 H100-equivalent GPUs (12-month term) with monthly billing.
- Price band (estimate): $XX,XXX–$YY,XXX / month depending on exact SKU and support tier. Final pricing will include a one-time onboarding fee and optional extended SLO coverage.
- Billing terms: net-60 available for enterprise customers; we can do a single PO + quarterly invoices if that helps internal accounting.
- SLA: Redwood proposes 99.5% uptime (credits structure in attached draft). We are open to negotiating tighter latency SLOs tied to measured workloads in the acceptance window.

Commercial asks for procurement: please provide
- Legal contact (name + email) for the MSA and PO routing.
- Any required contract templates or procurement forms to accelerate review.

Risk & policy notes for Heliox procurement to consider:
- Network egress & VPC peering: confirm whether Heliox will allow our controlled peering, or prefer VPN appliance.  Network topology can affect provisioning lead time.
- Data residency: default Redwood regions are US-west; if you need EU residency for any subset, flag now.

If procurement confirms contact + preferred provisioning start date, we will convert the draft SLA into a PO-ready attachment and hand off to Aditya for technical onboarding.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Marissa, Nikhil — thank you, this is great and aligns with our internal view. A few quick confirmations so procurement can move: 

- Procurement owner: Keisha Morgan <keisha.morgan@heliox.ai> (copied on this reply).
- Preferred provisioning start: June 14th. That puts onboarding sprint from Jun 14-25.
- Acceptance: we'll run Redwood's synthetic harness against a masked dataset; acceptance threshold 99th-token latency <= 420ms for initial go-live (we're willing to treat 400ms as stretch).
- Network: we'll do VPC peering. Security will share KMS key rotation requirements in a follow-up.

Keisha — could your team share a procurement PO template and lead time constraints? Also loop in legal if there are standard MSA edits we should expect.

Appreciate the speedy turn. We'll review the attachments and Keisha will take the PO ownership.

Best,
Olivia Chen
